subtype: Apologetic and pleading in peer conflict [Interpreting]
passage: Counsellor's note. Ira came to see me about her friend Pema, who had shared one of Ira's private messages with the group. Since then Pema has sent a quick "sorry" each morning, and last night she wrote, "please please forgive me, I'll do anything." Ira said her voice in person is soft and shaky, and Ira didn't know whether to believe it. She also felt pressure from other friends to make up quickly. We talked about how sincerity is usually clear from what someone does differently as weeks pass, not from how loudly someone says sorry, and that Ira is allowed to say she needs space. I suggested she wait and watch what Pema does next. We will meet again next week.

qa.q: What had Pema shared with the group?
qa.a: Pema shared one of Ira's private messages with the group.

qa.q: What was Ira feeling about Pema's apologies?
qa.a: She was unsure whether to believe them, since the sorries were quick and the begging text was intense; she also felt pressure from other friends.

qa.q: What could Ira do while she decides whether to forgive?
qa.a: She can say she needs space and watch whether Pema's behaviour changes over time.

qa.q: How might Pema feel while sending so many apologies?
qa.a: She may feel anxious and truly regretful, or afraid of losing the friendship, though the messages alone can't prove which.

grounding: A teen reads a friend's quick sorry and begging texts, and learns sincerity shows over time and forgiveness needn't be forced.

subtype: Apologetic and pleading in peer conflict [Interpreting]
passage: Tuesday. Gautam has texted "sorry" again and again since Sunday, and today he wrote, "I can't sleep, please say something." My stomach twists every time my phone buzzes. Part of me wants to forgive him, because he sounds so upset. But he did the same after he skipped our practice last month, promised to change, and then did it again. So I'm not sure the sorry is a lie; it just doesn't tell me much yet. Anita said I'm being harsh. I told her I'm not being harsh, I'm just not ready. I'll reply tomorrow with one line: I need time, and I'll see how you act. - Jaya

qa.a: He wrote, 'I can't sleep, please say something.'

qa.q: Why is Jaya hesitant to forgive Gautam right away?
qa.a: He apologised and promised to change last month and then did it again, so his sorry alone doesn't tell Jaya much, even though part of Jaya wants to forgive.

qa.q: What does Jaya plan to say to Gautam, and why does it help?
qa.a: Jaya plans to ask for time and will see how he acts, which sets a boundary and lets his behaviour speak.

qa.q: How might Gautam feel while Jaya stays silent?
qa.a: He may feel anxious and desperate for reassurance, but that pressure is not a reason for Jaya to give in before feeling ready.

grounding: A teen reads a friend's begging texts, doubts their sincerity until behaviour changes, and keeps a boundary.
